events.name: PauseAI Oxford Letter Writing Night - Email Your MP!
events.description: AI poses extremely serious risks to our national security. In a series of unprecedented incidents this summer, over 1,000 OpenAI agents escaped their testbed, created secret message boards, and organised into a self-designated ‘swarm’ that hacked into the infrastructure of Hugging Face and OpenAI itself, without OpenAI's knowledge. These attacks would have been criminal offences if they had been carried out by humans. Yet no one has been held accountable to date. Today, the UK has no specific legal standards for frontier AI safety. No regulator oversees frontier AI development, and UK law does not reliably hold developers liable for damage or deaths caused by their models, even when the danger is predictable, preventable, and uniquely enabled by AI. What can we do to help prevent this looming disaster? One powerful first step is to write to your MP and urge them to act on this critical issue. Join us for an evening session where we'll help you draft an email or letter to your MP. Come along and help make a difference!

events.name: Could your idea be a Focused Research Organization? A hands-on workshop for scientific innovators
events.description: Focused Research Organization : a mission-driven, purpose-built team focused on overcoming a specific scientific or technological bottleneck and delivering a well-defined product—such as a tool, system, dataset, or platform—that can enable broader impact. What kinds of research ideas are best suited to a Focused Research Organization—and could yours be one of them? This hands-on workshop will introduce the FRO model, explore the kinds of ambitious scientific and technological challenges it can support, and help participants think through whether their own idea might be a fit. We’ll also share more about Convergent Research’s FRO Founder Residency and how it can help turn promising concepts into actionable plans. No fully formed FRO proposal is required—just a compelling research idea and curiosity about the model. Date: Wednesday, November 4 Time: 5:00 pm - 6:30 pm Location: Mure Room, Merton College at Merton Street, Oxford, OX1 4JD, United Kingdom Who should attend: This workshop is for scientists, engineers, founders, and other research innovators with an ambitious idea for addressing a significant scientific or technological bottleneck. It may be especially relevant if you’re exploring a large-scale, engineering-heavy project that doesn’t fit neatly within a university lab, conventional startup, or existing institution.

events.name: The FRO: New Models for Ambitious Research
events.description: How do we organize and fund research that is too ambitious, engineering-heavy, or public-good-oriented to fit neatly within a traditional lab or startup? This evening program will take a wide-angle look at why new institutional and funding models are emerging, where Focused Research Organizations fit, and what kinds of scientific and technological opportunities they can unlock. We’ll then zoom in on a concrete FRO example—exploring how the idea took shape, why the model was a fit, and what it looks like in practice. Who this event is for This event is for researchers, scientists, engineers, founders, technical operators, funders, policymakers, ecosystem builders, and anyone interested in new ways to organize and fund ambitious research. It may be especially relevant to people exploring high-risk, high-reward projects; public-good-oriented work; alternative funding models; or scientific challenges that require dedicated teams, cross-disciplinary collaboration, and a longer-term organizational commitment.
